# Calling the game

<!-- Generated by `coney-tools pcsx2 recipe render` from research/pcsx2-recipes.toml. Do not edit. -->

One group of the [PCSX2 recipes](../pcsx2-recipes.md): how to run a recipe is on that page.

- [call](#call): Make the game call one of its own functions with up to six integer or pointer arguments.
- [lua](#lua): Run a Lua chunk in the level's script state, as a level script would: any script binding, any global.
- [lua-globals](#lua-globals): List the script's global variables (the mission script's state) whose names hold a
  pattern.
- [human-event](#human-event): Send a game event (an event record with an id) to a human: its script handler, its gang,
  then its brain.
- [uncuff](#uncuff): Start freeing a cuffed human by the mash, as triangle does, and read where the freer and the cuffed
  human stand.

## call {#call}

Make the game call one of its own functions with up to six integer or pointer arguments.

The `call-brains` hook sits at `Brains_Update`'s entry (`0x00293b28`, step 5 of the character step) and checks the call
block at `0x000af000` every update: the function's address at `+0x0` (0 when none waits), six arguments from `+0x4`
(passed in `a0`-`a3`, `t0`, `t1`), the result at `+0x1c` and a count of calls made at `+0x20`. The runner writes the
arguments, then the address; the hook clears the address, makes the call on the game's thread, stores `v0` and counts
it. Only integer and pointer arguments: a function that takes a float in `f12` gets whatever is there, so call such
functions through their script binding with `lua`. The state must have the hook installed (`pcsx2 prepare-state ...
--patch call-brains`) and the game must be running.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Parameters | `function` (expr): the function's address, such as 0x0041abe8; `a0` (expr, default `0`): first argument (an expression: 0x10, player, u32(player + 0x90)); `a1` (expr, default `0`): second argument; `a2` (expr, default `0`): third argument; `a3` (expr, default `0`): fourth argument |
| Preconditions | patches: `call-brains`; emulation running |
| Evidence | confirmed (runtime) |
| Ghidra | `0x00293b28 Brains_Update` |
| Research | [guides/research-traces.md#hooks](../research-traces.md#hooks) |
| Confirmed at runtime | 2026-10-21, copy `pcsx2-d`, PCSX2 2.9.129 (PCSX2-MCP fork), level99 street (slot 6); GetCheckPoint's worker 0x0041abe8 returned the checkpoint the game state holds |

```sh
uv run --project python coney-tools pcsx2 recipe run call --copy COPY --agent ID --arg function=<function> --arg a0=0 --arg a1=0 --arg a2=0 --arg a3=0
```

Steps:

```text
{ call = "function", args = ["a0", "a1", "a2", "a3"] }
{ show = "result", label = "result" }
```

## lua {#lua}

Run a Lua chunk in the level's script state, as a level script would: any script binding, any global.

`ScriptSystem *0x00512b04` holds the level's `lua_State` at `+0x04`; its vtable slot `+0x2c` is `ScriptSystem_DoString`
(`0x00356a78`), which runs a string with `lua_dobuffer`. The runner writes the code into spare memory at `0x000c0000`
(zeros in every state checked) and has the call hook call `ScriptSystem_DoString(system, code, 0)`; the result is 0 when
the chunk ran without error. A chunk can call every binding the level scripts use ([script
bindings](../../references/bindings/index.md)): `HuCreate`, `HuKill`, `GiveMoney`, `StatAdd`, `SetCheckPoint`,
`MenuLoadLevel`, `GoalFight`, `Teleport`, and the level's own functions (`P2.SetupLesson1()`). Lua 4 syntax: `local`,
`%upvalues`, no `#`. The text is a Python format string: `{name}` takes a bound value, so write a Lua table
constructor's braces doubled, `{{x, y, z}}`.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Parameters | `code` (text): the Lua chunk, such as 'GiveMoney(100)' |
| Preconditions | patches: `call-brains`; emulation running |
| Evidence | confirmed (runtime) |
| Ghidra | `0x00356a78 ScriptSystem_DoString`, `0x00293b28 Brains_Update` |
| Research | [research/scripting.md](../../research/scripting.md), [guides/research-traces.md#hooks](../research-traces.md#hooks) |
| Confirmed at runtime | 2026-10-21, copy `pcsx2-d`, PCSX2 2.9.129 (PCSX2-MCP fork), level99 street (slot 6); set a global and read it back with lua-globals; GiveMoney(5) took the inventory money from 191 to 196 |

```sh
uv run --project python coney-tools pcsx2 recipe run lua --copy COPY --agent ID --arg code=<code>
```

Steps:

```text
{ lua = "{code}" }
{ show = "result", label = "lua_dobuffer" }
```

## lua-globals {#lua-globals}

List the script's global variables (the mission script's state) whose names hold a pattern.

The globals table is `ScriptSystem *0x00512b04` -> `lua_State` `+0x04` -> globals `+0x44`. A Lua 4 table (`Hash`) holds
its node array at `+0x0` and its node count as the `u16` at `+0x6` (the `u16` at `+0x4` is its tag, 4); a node is 40
bytes: the key `TObject` (type at `+0x0`, value at `+0x8`), the value `TObject` at `+0x10` (type `+0x10`, value `+0x18`)
and the chain pointer at `+0x20`. Types: 1 nil, 2 number (a double), 3 string (its text at `+0x10` of the string), 4
table, 5 function. Level scripts keep their state in globals (`bWarriorsFight`, `vFenceSection`), so this shows how far
a mission has gone. A table value prints as its address; its nodes read the same way.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Parameters | `pattern` (text): part of the names to show (case ignored); empty for all |
| Preconditions | patches: none; running or paused |
| Evidence | confirmed (runtime) |
| Ghidra | `0x00356a78 ScriptSystem_DoString`, `0x00328a30 Lua_CallCClosure` |
| Research | [research/scripting.md](../../research/scripting.md), [guides/research-tools.md#driving-pcsx2](../research-tools.md#driving-pcsx2) |
| Confirmed at runtime | 2026-10-21, copy `pcsx2-d`, PCSX2 2.9.129 (PCSX2-MCP fork), level99 street (slot 6); 1505 globals with a non-nil value; the node count u16 at +0x6 read 3500 (0xdac) and the node array held valid nodes up to there |

```sh
uv run --project python coney-tools pcsx2 recipe run lua-globals --copy COPY --agent ID --arg pattern=<pattern>
```

Steps:

```text
{ globals = "pattern" }
```

## human-event {#human-event}

Send a game event (an event record with an id) to a human: its script handler, its gang, then its brain.

`Human_OnEvent` (`0x0021d480`, human vtable `0x0053f088` slot `+0x44`) delivers an event record to the human's Lua
message handler (`ScriptHandler_Deliver` `0x00384c38`, which reads the id at `+0x20`), then to its gang (`Gang_OnEvent`
`0x00164c20`), then to its brain (`Brain_OnEvent` `0x0028f928`), stopping at the first that consumes it; the result is 1
when one consumed it. The brain's own handler is the function at brain `+0x28` (with `this` adjusted by the `s16` at
`+0x24`): `WarriorBrain_OnEvent` `0x003063b0` for a Warrior, `PlayerBrain_OnEvent` `0x00303e90` for the player. The
runner builds a record at `0x000c8000` (spare memory): `+0x00` the human who caused it, as the human's address
(confirmed at runtime for event `0xb`, which a Warrior keeps at brain `+0x27c`), `+0x04` the other party, `+0x20` the
event id ([the event record](../../research/ai-brain-types.md#event-record): 0 the prompt, 1 hit (with `+0x11` set to
count as an attack), 2 reset, `0xb` a new enemy, ...). The brain's goals may be refilled in the same update, so check an
effect that stays (a Warrior's noted enemy, its target).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Parameters | `who` (human): the human's name; empty for the player; `event` (number): the event id (ai-brain-types.md#event-record); `causer` (expr, default `0`): record +0x00: the human who caused it (an address), 0 none; `other` (expr, default `0`): record +0x04: the other party, 0 none |
| Preconditions | patches: `call-brains`; emulation running |
| Evidence | confirmed (runtime) |
| Ghidra | `0x0021d480 Human_OnEvent`, `0x0028f928 Brain_OnEvent`, `0x00384c38 ScriptHandler_Deliver` |
| Research | [research/ai-brain-types.md#event-record](../../research/ai-brain-types.md#event-record), [research/ai/index.md#events](../../research/ai/index.md#events) |
| Confirmed at runtime | 2026-10-21, copy `pcsx2-d`, PCSX2 2.9.129 (PCSX2-MCP fork), level99 street (slot 6); event 0xb to Ash (a Warrior) with Civilians2 as causer: consumed, brain +0x27c held Civilians2's address and +0x280 was 1 |

```sh
uv run --project python coney-tools pcsx2 recipe run human-event --copy COPY --agent ID --arg who=<who> --arg event=<event> --arg causer=0 --arg other=0
```

Steps:

```text
{ let = { h = "who", record = "0x000c8000" } }
{ write = "record + 0x00", type = "u32", value = "causer" }
{ write = "record + 0x04", type = "u32", value = "other" }
{ write = "record + 0x08", type = "u32", value = "0" }
{ write = "record + 0x0c", type = "u32", value = "0" }
{ write = "record + 0x10", type = "u32", value = "0" }
{ write = "record + 0x14", type = "u32", value = "0" }
{ write = "record + 0x18", type = "u32", value = "0" }
{ write = "record + 0x1c", type = "u32", value = "0" }
{ write = "record + 0x20", type = "u32", value = "event" }
{ write = "record + 0x24", type = "u32", value = "0" }
{ show = "u32(brain(h) + 0x28)", label = "brain_handler" }
{ call = "0x0021d480", args = ["h", "record"] }
{ show = "result", label = "consumed", format = "int" }
```

## uncuff {#uncuff}

Start freeing a cuffed human by the mash, as triangle does, and read where the freer and the cuffed human stand.

`Uncuff_Start` (`0x00260ca8`, the mash path of the kind-0 record's triangle,
[Uncuffing](../../research/crimes.md#uncuffing)) refuses unless the cuffed human is cuffed and not already held
`0x10000`; then the freer says 68, is steered by `Attack_SteerToTarget` (`0x002761c8`) for clip 325 over 0.1 s, his
action becomes `0x15`, `Uncuff_BeginMash` (`0x0022d3f8`) starts mode 1 and the two play 325 into 329 and 326 into 330,
the cuffed human's partner (`+0xc8`) becoming the freer (as a handle, not the address). The recipe makes the call
through the call hook with the freer and the cuffed human, so it skips the record's own checks (the 0.2 m capsule test,
the record's user) and the mash meter; put the freer next to the cuffed human first (`teleport`). It reads both humans'
positions and headings before, two waited updates after the call (the steer's three updates done, the call's own update
counted: the freer at 325's reach from the cuffed human, turned so that he lies along 325's direction) and 30 updates
after (325's root turn done: the freer facing him). The cuffed human does not move or turn. Circle (a quit command) ends
the mash; with no input it never ends, as the decay waits for a first L1 or R1.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Parameters | `freer` (human): the freer's name; empty for the player; `cuffed` (human): the cuffed human's name |
| Preconditions | patches: `call-brains`; emulation running |
| Evidence | confirmed (runtime) |
| Ghidra | `0x00260ca8 Uncuff_Start`, `0x002761c8 Attack_SteerToTarget`, `0x0022d3f8 Uncuff_BeginMash` |
| Research | [research/crimes.md#uncuff-pose](../../research/crimes.md#uncuff-pose), [research/crimes.md#uncuffing](../../research/crimes.md#uncuffing) |
| Confirmed at runtime | 2026-10-21, copy `pcsx2-b`, PCSX2 2.9.129 (PCSX2-MCP fork), level80 checkpoint 2, Snow and Cowboy cuffed (loaded from slot 6 with load-checkpoint); Cleon put at (-196.0, 231.65) facing 0 by Snow: 3 updates later 0.747 m from him at -2.36 degrees, 30 later at -83.34 degrees; Snow never moved |

```sh
uv run --project python coney-tools pcsx2 recipe run uncuff --copy COPY --agent ID --arg freer=<freer> --arg cuffed=<cuffed>
```

Steps:

```text
{ let = { f = "freer", c = "cuffed" } }
{ show = "f32(tf(f) + 0x0)", label = "freer_x" }
{ show = "f32(tf(f) + 0x4)", label = "freer_y" }
{ show = "wrap(deg(heading(f)))", label = "freer_heading_deg" }
{ show = "f32(tf(c) + 0x0)", label = "cuffed_x" }
{ show = "f32(tf(c) + 0x4)", label = "cuffed_y" }
{ show = "wrap(deg(heading(c)))", label = "cuffed_heading_deg" }
{ call = "0x00260ca8", args = ["f", "c"] }
{ wait = 2 }
{ show = "hypot(f32(tf(f) + 0x0) - f32(tf(c) + 0x0), f32(tf(f) + 0x4) - f32(tf(c) + 0x4))", label = "steered_distance" }
{ show = "wrap(deg(heading(f)))", label = "steered_heading_deg" }
{ wait = 28 }
{ show = "f32(tf(f) + 0x0)", label = "freer_x" }
{ show = "f32(tf(f) + 0x4)", label = "freer_y" }
{ show = "wrap(deg(heading(f)))", label = "freer_heading_deg" }
{ show = "f32(tf(c) + 0x0)", label = "cuffed_x" }
{ show = "f32(tf(c) + 0x4)", label = "cuffed_y" }
{ show = "wrap(deg(heading(c)))", label = "cuffed_heading_deg" }
```
